title: Red Team Member (I) (Col to Capt) FMOS, DC CD&I
raw_text:
3.     MOS 0506, Red Team Member (I) (Col to Capt) FMOS, DC CD&I

    a. Summary. Red Team Members provide commanders with an independent
capability to fully explore alternatives in plans, operations, and
capabilities in the context of the operational environment and from the
perspective of both our partners and adversaries. They promote staff self-
awareness and help frame problems and questions, manage small groups,
integrate staff planning, close communication gaps amongst the staff, and
help the staff become aware of potential cognitive biases and logic
fallacies. Red Team Members serve at Headquarters Marine Corps, Training and
Education Command, Marine Corps University, MAGTF Staff Training Program, MEF
staffs, MEB staffs and the U.S. Army’s University of Foreign Military and
Cultural Studies.

    b. Prerequisites. Security requirement: adjudicated NACLC secret
security clearance with eligibility for access to top secret (TS) and TS-
sensitive compartmented information (SCI).

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete a course taught by MCU red team instructors that meets
the Army Foreign Military and Cultural Studies Standard.

            (2) MOS will be assigned by EDCOM upon completion of the course.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Provide critical reviews and analysis of concepts and plans
(classified and unclassified) as well as providing alternative and creative
solutions.

        (2) Anticipate the cultural perception of partners, adversaries and
others by identifying the second and third order effects of operations in a
cultural context and anticipating strategic and operational implications.


                                          1-31                       Enclosure (1)
 1108                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



        (3) Improve decision making during planning and operations by
assisting in the development of problem definition and desired end states,
identifying friendly and enemy vulnerabilities, challenging assumptions and
offering alternative perspectives.

        (4) Lead Red Teams during OPTs or serve as a facilitator for Red
Teaming of special projects, policies, initiatives, or other command-directed
activities.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

Supervise staff, training them, planning their work, and evaluating their performance.

They promote staff self- awareness and help frame problems and questions, manage small groups, integrate staff planning, close communication gaps amongst the staff, and help the staff become aware of potential cognitive biases and logic fallacies.

(2) MOS will be assigned by EDCOM upon completion of the course.
Plan, supervise, and review work of assigned subordinates.
d. Duties (1) Provide critical reviews and analysis of concepts and plans (classified and unclassified) as well as providing alternative and creative solutions.
Analyze worker or production problems and recommend solutions, such as improving production methods or implementing motivational plans.

Supervise, train, or mentor junior team members.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
